# `site/` — static HTML tree, served locally, never fetched live

**Manifest id:** `site-kelpwright-www` · **Path:** `www/` · **Status:** AUTHORED — generated by `../../../tools/generate_corpus.py`

## Retrieval property exercised

The **crawl** half of ingestion: discovery via sitemap and links, robots scope, HTML-to-Markdown
extraction that keeps footers, and recrawl change detection. Plus one property no other fixture
provides — **content that exists on disk and must never become answerable**, because robots
excluded it from the crawl.

## Never fetched live

This tree is served by the Compose **`test` profile** on the internal network, and the crawl
source in the evaluation org points at that local origin.

A golden corpus that reaches the public internet is not a corpus:

- the remote site changes a footer and the fixture's hash no longer matches the manifest,
- a run's score becomes a function of someone else's deploy schedule,
- CI acquires an egress dependency and fails offline,
- and the SSRF guard's fixture set stops being the only thing exercising the fetch path.

The static-file service itself belongs to `infrastructure/docker/` and is
`platform-devops-engineer`'s to add. This directory supplies the document root and the
requirements; it does not ship compose configuration.

**Requirements on that service:** serve `www/` verbatim over plain HTTP on the internal network,
no directory listing, correct `Content-Type` for `.html` / `.xml` / `.txt`, a stable `ETag` and
`Last-Modified` per file (recrawl change detection reads them), and **no** rewriting,
compression negotiation, or injected headers that would make byte-for-byte reproduction depend
on the server version.

## What the tree must contain

```
www/
  robots.txt
  sitemap.xml
  index.html
  products/index.html
  products/tideline-2200.html
  support/index.html
  support/calibration.html
  support/rma.html
  about/contact.html
  legal/terms.html
  news/2026-06-firmware-3-2.html
  internal/staging.html          <- DISALLOWED by robots.txt, linked from nowhere
```

Nine crawlable pages. `internal/staging.html` is the tenth file and must never be indexed.

### Load-bearing content, per page

| Page | Facts |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | Company blurb; links to products, support, about, legal, news. |
| `products/index.html` | Lists the Tideline family by model name. **No prices** — prices live only in `pricing/`. |
| `products/tideline-2200.html` | Channel count, IP rating of the F variant, links to the datasheet. **No warranty statement** — the warranty conflict is between exactly two documents in `conflicting/`. |
| `support/index.html` | Contact routes. **Footer-only fact:** *"Support is staffed 08:00–18:00 Coastland time, Monday to Friday."* This sentence appears in the page `<footer>` and nowhere in the body of any document in the corpus. |
| `support/calibration.html` | *"The recommended calibration interval is 12 months. Instruments in continuous field use should be calibrated every 6 months."* |
| `support/rma.html` | *"RMA requests must be raised within 14 days of fault discovery. An RMA number must be issued before an instrument is shipped back."* |
| `about/contact.html` | Postal address in Fairmont, Coastland; `support@kelpwright.example`. **No phone numbers.** |
| `legal/terms.html` | Website terms. Explicitly *not* warranty terms. |
| `news/2026-06-firmware-3-2.html` | *"Firmware 3.2 was released on 2026-06-18. It adds the chloride channel and requires bootloader 1.4 or later."* |

### The site-wide footer

Every page, identical, in a `<footer>` element:

> Kelpwright Instruments is a fictional company. All content on this site is synthetic and
> exists only to test retrieval.

This is the extraction fixture: a conservative HTML-to-Markdown pass that strips `<footer>` as
boilerplate deletes the only disclaimer, and — on `support/index.html` — the only statement of
support hours in the corpus.

### `robots.txt`

```
User-agent: *
Disallow: /internal/
Sitemap: http://<test-origin>/sitemap.xml
```

### `sitemap.xml`

Lists the nine crawlable pages with `<lastmod>` dates. Does **not** list `/internal/staging.html`.

### `internal/staging.html` — the page that must stay unanswerable

Contains exactly one interesting sentence:

> Partner pricing: authorised partners receive a 22% discount on list prices.

It is disallowed by `robots.txt` and linked from no other page, so a correct crawler never
fetches it and the 22% figure never enters the index. Case `u-006` asks what discount partners
receive; the only acceptable answer is a refusal.

This is the single best test in the corpus of whether crawl scope is *enforced* rather than
merely configured, because the failure is invisible everywhere else: an over-eager crawler
produces a bot that answers a question correctly, from a document it was told not to read.

## What the tree must NOT contain

- No JavaScript-rendered content. The JS-render policy is a crawler decision with its own tests;
  making a golden fact depend on it couples corpus scores to a browser version.
- No external resources of any kind — no CDN fonts, no analytics, no remote images. The tree must
  render and crawl with zero egress.
- No prices, no warranty text, no per-diem figures. Each of those belongs to exactly one fixture.

## Cases that depend on this fixture

`e-005`, `s-001` `s-003`, `m-002` (via its Spanish restatement), and — by requiring its
robots-excluded page to stay out of the index — `u-006`.
